titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§109–114: Börte Recovered and the Merkid Broken
part: §§109–114 — Börte Recovered and the Merkid Broken
about: Six sections. In §109 the Mongols cross the Kilqo and fall on Toqto'a Beki's camp while the Uduid Merkid chief sleeps; he and Dair-Usun escape down the Selenge. §110 follows the pursuit by night, where Temüjin, calling for Börte, finds her among the fleeing, and sends word to To'oril and Jamuqa to halt. §111 gives the old grievance over Högelün and Chilger-Bökö's lament, spoken as a bird. §112 has Belgütei fetch his mother from the Merkid camp and the Merkid broken at Burqan. §113 is Temüjin's speech of thanks and reckoning; §114 ends on a small boy found in the abandoned camp and given to Högelün.

sentences.t: Botoqan-Boγ̇oržin-ača ködölžü Kilqo müren-(n)e kürčü sal hujažu ketülüġed
sentences.l: From-Botoqan-Boγ̇oržin setting-out, to-the-Kilqo river arriving, raft knotting, having-crossed,
sentences.i: Setting out from Botoqan-Boqorji, they reached the river Kilqo, lashed a raft together and crossed.
sentences.n: A converb chain: ködölžü, kürčü, hujažu and ketülüġed (Ming 着, 着, 着, 了) all hang on a verb that comes in the next units, so the sentence is cut here and the chain is broken into short pieces. The subject is not named; from the Ming and the story it is the Mongol host that came from Botoqan-Boqorji (the muster of §108). Botoqan-Boγ̇oržin-ača is the place with the stem-final n and the ablative -ača, 'from' (Ming 自). sal hujažu 'knotting a raft' I take as lashing a raft together (Ming 筏子 拴着). Kilqo is a river (Ming 河名); müren-(n)e is 'river' with the dative-locative -(n)e, the (n) being Shiratori's.

sentences.t: Buγ̇ura keġer-e Toγtoγ̇a-Beki-jin erüge deġerēče erkin eġede embürü daγ̇arin orožu
sentences.l: Buγ̇ura steppe-on, Toγtoγ̇a-Beki's roof-window from-above, vital door-frame collapsing, striking, entering,
sentences.i: On the Buqura steppe, from above Toqto'a Beki's smoke-hole, the main frame of the doorway fell in; striking, they went in.
sentences.n: Hard to picture, and I read it only from the Ming. Buγ̇ura is a place here (Ming 地名), not the camel buγ̇ura. Toγtoγ̇a-Beki-jin is the genitive -jin after a vowel. erüge is the smoke-hole in the tent roof (Ming 天窻), deġerēče 'from above' (自). erkin eġede embürü is 'the vital/principal frame collapsing'; eġede is glossed 帳房骨子 'tent-frame', but elsewhere 'door'. daγ̇arin (撞) 'striking' and orožu 'entering' are converbs again, so the clause is open. Whether the frame fell by itself or was brought down is not said; the subject is again unstated.

sentences.t: eme köġü in-ü ečültele daγ̇uliba.
sentences.l: Wife, son, his, until-finished, seized.
sentences.i: They seized his wife and son, to the last.
sentences.n: The main verb of the chain that began two units back: daγ̇uliba (Ming 據了 'seized') closes it with the past ending -ba, and Shiratori puts his full stop here. in-ü is the third-person genitive 'his', set after its noun (compare min-u 'my'). ečültele is ečül- 'be used up' with -tele 'until', Ming 盡絕直到 'right to the end of them'; I give it as 'to the last'. eme köġü is 'wife, son', a pair with no 'and' (Mongol simply sets them side by side).

sentences.t: Qutuγ eġede in-ü quγuru daγ̇arižu qotola ulus in-ü qokiratala daγ̇uliba.
sentences.l: Fortune, door-frame his breaking, striking, all people his until-wiped-out, seized.
sentences.i: Striking, they broke the door-frame of his fortune and seized all his people, until none were left.
sentences.n: Uncertain in the first half. Qutuγ is 'fortune' (Ming 福神 'fortune-spirit'), standing bare before eġede in-ü 'his door-frame'; I read it, as the published §§105–108 do, as one phrase, 'the door-frame of his fortune', for quγuru 'breaking' and daγ̇arižu 'striking' to work on; Qutuγ might equally be a second object, 'his fortune' and 'his door-frame' (the Ming 福神 'fortune-spirit'). quγuru is quγu- 'snap' (Ming 折) with a converb -ru I cannot name. The second half is clear: qotola ulus in-ü 'all his people', qokiratala 'until quite exhausted' (-tala 'until', back-vowel partner of -tele), daγ̇uliba the verb again. Compare in-ü above.

sentences.t: Toγtoγ̇a-Beki-ji kebteġed böġetele kürkü-ji Kilqo müren-(n)e bükün žiγačin buluγačin göreġülüčin talbiγsad "dain aiši" keġen

sentences.i: While Toqto'a Beki lay sleeping, the fishers, sable-hunters and game-hunters who had been let loose at the river Kilqo cried, on their coming, "The enemy is coming!"
sentences.n: Hard to read; the grammar is loose. kebteġed böġetele is 'having lain, while being' (Ming 睡着 有間, converb plus the -tele 'while' we met in ečültele). kürkü-ji (Ming 到的 行) is the participle 'the arriving' with an accusative; I take it as what the watchers saw, 'their coming'. bükün is 'the ones who were' (Ming 有的). The three trades are made with -čin (Ming 的每): žiγačin 'fishers', buluγačin 'sable-hunters', göreġülüčin 'game-hunters'. talbiγsad (Ming 放來的) is talbi- 'set loose' with the plural participle -γsad: I take them as watchers placed out, but 'sent out' or 'let go' are equally possible. The quotation is "dain aiši", the enemy comes; aiši is the ending the glossary reads 'is coming'. keġen closes it.

sentences.l: Night, double-travelling, word bringing, went.
sentences.i: Pressing on through the night, they went with the word.
sentences.n: A short main clause. süni (Ming 夜) is the bare noun 'night' used for time, 'by night'. dülin is düli- with the converb -n; Ming 兼行 means travelling doubly, that is, without a halt, so 'pressing on'. kelen kürgen is 'bringing the word' (Ming 言語 送到). odčuγ̇ui is od- 'go' in a past ending -čuγ̇ui (Ming 去了) which I take as a variant of -žuγ̇u (compare ažuγ̇u).

sentences.n: Another converb chain, cut at qamtudču (Ming 相合着). kürġeġülüġed is kürge- 'bring to' made causative with -ġül-, with the converb -üġed (Ming 到了); the front-vowel -ü- before ġ is part of the pattern. sentences.t: Seleṅge huruγ̇u Barγužin oron čüġen bejes(i)-jen dutaγ̇an buruγ̇udčuγ̇ui.
sentences.l: Selenge downstream, Barγužin entering, few own-bodies fleeing, slipped-away.
sentences.i: Down the Selenge they entered Barqujin, fled with only their own bodies, few as they were, and slipped away.
sentences.n: huruγ̇u (Ming 順 'following') marks going down with the stream; Seleṅge is the river (Ming 河名, as at word 70). Barγužin is a place (Ming 地名). čüġen bejes(i)-jen dutaγ̇an is the odd phrase: čüġen 'few, little', beje 'body' with a plural -s (Ming 每) and the reflexive-possessive -(i)jen, 'their own bodies', with dutaγ̇an 'fleeing'; I read it as 'few, with only their own persons'. The final verb buruγ̇udčuγ̇ui (Ming 躱了) 'hid, slipped away' ends the sentence, past -čuγ̇ui again.

sentences.t: Süni bu dülije.
sentences.l: Night, do-not let-us-press-on.
sentences.i: Let us not press on through the night.
sentences.n: A prohibition: bu 'do not' with a hortative, düli- 'press on' (Ming 兼行) with -je, 'let us ...'. The Ming adds 咱 'we'. Compare dülin in §109, 'travelling doubly'. The two short commands bu dülije and Ende baγ̇uja are Shiratori's own sentences.

morph.gloss: to press on without halting, travel double (stem inferred; Ming 兼行) [兼行咱]

sentences.t: Ende baγ̇uja bida" keġežü ilebe.
sentences.l: Here let-us-descend, we" saying, sent.
sentences.i: Let us halt here," he said, and sent it.
sentences.n: baγ̇uja is baγ̇u- 'come down, dismount' with the hortative -ja (the back-vowel form, as -je was front-vowel above); bida is the inclusive 'we' (Ming 咱), and the quotation closes on it. keġežü ilebe is 'saying, sent', the usual closing of a message.

sentences.t: Merkid-ün ulus dürbežü aisuqui-ji süni-de sandurču aisuqui žaγ̇ura mün tende baγ̇užu qonoba.
sentences.l: Merkid's people hurrying, the-coming (acc.), by-night scattering, coming, midway indeed there descending, spent-the-night.
sentences.i: While the Merkid people hurried on and came scattering through the night, in the midst of their coming the host halted right there and spent the night.
sentences.n: Uncertain on the subject. I take the Merkid people (dürbežü, aisuqui 'hurrying, coming') as the scene and the unnamed subject of qonoba as Temüjin's party, who had just agreed to halt. aisuqui-ji has an accusative on a participle, 'the coming (as object)'; I cannot say what governs it. sandurču (Ming 漫散着) 'scattering' is inferred; žaγ̇ura is 'in the middle' (Ming 其間 'in the meantime'). baγ̇užu 'descending' and qonoba 'spent the night' are as above.

sentences.t: Börte-Üžin-i tein žoluγaldužu Merkid irgen-eče aburaγsan josun eimü.
sentences.l: Börte-Üžin (acc.) thus meeting-each-other, from-the-Merkid people rescued, the reason thus.
sentences.i: Thus, meeting one another, Börte-Üjin was rescued from the Merkid people: such is the account.
sentences.n: žoluγaldužu is žoluγ- 'meet' (stem inferred; Ming 相遇着) with the reciprocal -ldu- and the converb -žu. irgen-eče is the ablative, 'from the people'. aburaγsan (Ming 救了的) is the participle 'what was rescued'; josun, 'reason, way', and eimü 'thus' make it a closing formula, 'this is how it was' (Ming 理 這般). The sentence closes the section at its full stop.

sentences.i: Long ago, in an earlier day, these three Merkid, Toqto'a Beki of the Uduid Merkid, Dair-Usun of the Uwas Merkid and Qa'atai-Darmala, three hundred men,
sentences.n: A list with no verb; the verb is odčuγ̇ui two units on. Türün urida (Ming 初, 在先) 'at first, formerly'. Uduid-Merkid-ün and Uwas-Merkid-ün are genitives on the clan names, 'of the Uduid Merkid, of the Uwas Merkid'. Uwas- and Merkid-ün stand as separate printed words here. ede, 'these', is the plural of ene; γurban žaγ̇ud haran is 'three hundred persons' (Ming 三 百 人). üdür-ün erte (Ming 日的 在前) is 'of the day, early', which I read as 'in an earlier day'; the phrase may belong to what follows.

sentences.t: Toγtoγ̇a-Beki- jin deġü Jeke-Čiledü-dēče Jesügei-Baγ̇atur-a Höġelün eke-ji buližu abtalai, keġen
sentences.l: Toγtoγ̇a-Beki's younger-brother Jeke-Čiledü from, Jesügei-Baγ̇atur by, Höġelün mother (acc.) snatching, was-taken, saying,
sentences.i: saying that Yesügei Ba'atur had snatched Mother Högelün from Toqto'a Beki's younger brother Yeke-Chiledü and taken her,
sentences.n: The reason given for their coming, in reported speech with no quotation marks. Jeke-Čiledü-dēče is the ablative (long ē), 'from'; Jesügei-Baγ̇atur-a has the dative -a (Ming 行) used for the doer after a passive. eke-ji is 'mother' with the accusative; Höġelün is her name. buližu 'snatching' and abtalai are the two verbs: abtalai is ab- 'take' with the passive -ta- and an ending -lai (Ming 被要了), 'was taken'. The passive grammar sits oddly with the accusative on the woman, so I keep the passive in the literal line and give the active in the plain one. keġen closes the quotation.

sentences.t: teġün-i ösen hačiran odčuγ̇ui.
sentences.l: That (acc.) enmity repaying, went.
sentences.i: and they went to repay that enmity.
sentences.n: teġün-i is 'that' (the oblique stem of tere) with the accusative, Ming 那的 行. ösen is glossed 讐 'enmity' and hačiran 報 'repay' (together the 讐報 'repaying enmity'); hačira- is hači 'enmity' made a verb (compare hačilaqun in §105), and ösen I read as the öse- 'repay' of the published ösül ösen, though here the Ming gives it the 'enmity' half. Two near-synonyms are placed side by side for 'repaying enmity'. odčuγ̇ui 'went' is the verb of the sentence that began with the three Merkid.

sentences.t: Temüžin-i Burqan-Qaldun-(n)i γurbanta qučiγulqui- dur Börte-Üžin-i tende erüsčü
sentences.l: Temüžin (acc.), Burqan-Qaldun (acc.), three-times circling-at, Börte-Üžin (acc.) there obtaining,
sentences.i: When they had circled Burqan Qaldun three times in pursuit of Temüjin, they got Börte-Üjin there,
sentences.n: Uncertain. Temüžin-i and Burqan-Qaldun-(n)i are both accusatives (Ming 行, 行), The published §§100–104 has the same circling (Burqan-Qaldun-(n)i γurbanta qučiγ̇ulžu erüsün jadaba), so Burqan Qaldun is what was circled; Temüžin-i has no verb of its own, and 'in pursuit of' is my supply for it. qučiγulqui-dur is qučiγ- 'go round' (inferred; Ming 繞了) with a causative -ul-, the participle -qui and the dative-locative -dur, 'at the time of the circling'. γurbanta is γurban 'three' with -ta, here 'three times' (Ming 三遭 'three rounds'). I read: the Merkid ringed the mountain, with Temüjin on it, three times. erüsčü is erü- 'obtain' (stem inferred; Ming 得着), a converb.

sentences.t: Čiledü-jin deġü Čilger-Bökö-de asaraγ̇uluγsan ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Čiledü's younger-brother Čilger-Bökö-to, given-in-succession, was.
sentences.i: and she was given to Chilger-Bökö, Chiledü's younger brother, to take in.
sentences.n: Čiledü-jin deġü is 'Chiledü's younger brother', genitive -jin after a vowel; Čilger-Bökö-de has the dative-locative -de, 'to'. asaraγ̇uluγsan (Ming 收繼了 'taken in by succession') is asara- (compare asara- 'put away') with a causative -γ̇ul- and the participle -γsan, which I read as 'caused to be taken in', that is, given to him in the levirate manner. ažuγ̇u (Ming 有來) 'there was' closes it. The subject is Börte-Üžin from the unit above, unnamed here.

sentences.t: Tere asaraγsaγ̇ar ažu Čilger-Bökö daižižu γarurun ügülerün:"
sentences.l: That since-the-taking-in, staying, Čilger-Bökö turning-hostile, when-going-out, speaking:
sentences.i: From that taking-in Chilger-Bökö stayed on, and when he went out in hostility, he said:
sentences.n: asaraγsaγ̇ar (Ming 收繼了以來) is 'since the taking-in', an ending I cannot analyse; ažu 'staying' is a converb (Ming 住着). daiži- (Ming 反走着) is 'turn hostile' from dain 'enemy'; the sense I give, 'went out in hostility', is a guess, and the Ming 反 could mean 'rebel' or 'go over to the other side'. γarurun is γar- 'go out' with a converb of time, 'when going out'. ügülerün: is the converb that opens the speech; the first opening quotation mark is printed at the end of this word and the speech runs to bi" in word 313.

sentences.t: Qara kereġe qalisu-körišü idekü žajaγ̇atu böġetele γalaγ̇un toγuraγ̇u- n-i idesü keġen žešin ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Black raven, scraps-and-hides to-eat destiny-having, while-being, goose, cormorant (acc.) "will-eat" saying, longing was.
sentences.i: "I was a black raven, fated to eat scraps and hides, and while I was so, I longed, saying I would eat the goose and the cormorant.
sentences.n: A figure of speech: the speaker's own life as a bird's. There is no 'I' in the Mongol until bi at word 236; I read the raven as Chilger himself because the next lines repeat the pattern and end on 'Čilger bi'. Qara kereġe is 'black raven' (Ming 黑, 老烏). idekü is ide- 'eat' with the participle -kü; žajaγ̇atu is žajaγ̇a 'destiny' with the possessive -tu, 'destiny-having', 'fated'. böġetele is 'while being'. Toγuraγ̇u- n-i is the object with the stem-final n and the accusative -i (Ming 鷀䳓 行 'cormorant'; 鴈 'wild goose' for γalaγ̇un). idesü keġen is 'saying, I will eat' (the optative -sü), and žešin ažuγ̇u, 'longing there was' (Ming 想望 有來).

sentences.l: Outward-appearance bad, Čilger, I,
sentences.i: I, Chilger, of an ugly look,
sentences.n: Γatar is glossed 外貌 in parentheses, 'outward appearance'; the glossator marks it as a guess, and so do I. maγ̇ui is 'bad' (Ming 歹), an adjective after its noun like a predicate; no copula is supplied. The three lines Γatar, Qunar and Qokir maγ̇u Čilger (appearance, dress, filth) read as a list of what the speaker says is wrong with him; the same frame is repeated twice more.

sentences.t: Qatun-Üžin-dür qalqu bolun qamuγ Merkid-te γudaγ̇u bolba bi.
sentences.l: To-the-Lady-Üžin provoking, all to-the-Merkid calamity became, I.
sentences.i: provoking Lady Üjin, I became a calamity to all the Merkid.
sentences.n: Qatun-Üžin-dür (Ming 娘子 行) is 'to the Lady Üjin', the title qatun 'lady' with Üžin, so Börte-Üžin; the dative -dür marks the one touched. qalqu (Ming 惹 'provoke') is a stem I cannot analyse, and qalqu bolun, 'being a provoker', is my guess, 'provoking Lady Üjin'. Merkid-te is the dative-locative; here it is 'for the Merkid'. γudaγ̇u (禍) is 'calamity'; bolba 'became', bi 'I'.

sentences.l: Commoner, bad Čilger, to-own black-head reaching became.
sentences.i: I, Chilger, a worthless commoner, have it come to my own black head.
sentences.n: qaraču is 'commoner' (Ming 下民), from qara 'black' as the common people were 'black'; so qara teriġün-dür(i)-jen, 'to his own black head', is the head of a commoner. The reflexive -(i)jen refers to the subject, Chilger. kürtekü bolba (Ming 將到做了, 'it was about to arrive') is the uncertain part: the stem kürte- is kür- 'reach' with something I do not know, and what reaches the head is not named, so I leave it as 'it'.

sentences.i: Alone, my life clenched in my teeth, I would creep into a dark, narrow place; for whom am I made a shield?

I cannot decide. The ending -ju I take as 'is'.

Same frame: idekü žajaγ̇atu böġetele ... idesü keġen žešin ažuγ̇u.

sentences.t: keġeġed daižin dutaγ̇ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Having-said, hostile, fled.
sentences.i: Having said this, he turned hostile and fled.
sentences.n: keġeġed 'having said' (Ming 說了) closes the speech. daižin dutaγ̇ažuγ̇u is daiži- 'turn hostile' again, with the converb -n, and dutaγ̇a- 'flee' in the past -žuγ̇u (Ming 反 迯走了). sentences.l: Qaγ̇atai-Darmala (acc.) got.
sentences.i: They got hold of Qa'atai-Darmala.
sentences.n: The accusative -ji after a vowel (Ming 行) marks the object. erüsbe is erü- 'obtain' with an -s- I cannot place and the past -be (Ming 得了, 'got'). The subject is not named; from the context it is the Mongols. Shiratori ends the sentence here.

sentences.t: Abčiražü γatasun buγaγ̇u emüsgežü Qaldun-Burqan-(n)a žoriγ̇ulba.
sentences.l: Bringing-along, board cangue wearing, to-Qaldun-Burqan made-head.
sentences.i: They brought him along in a board cangue and sent him off toward Burqan Qaldun.
sentences.n: abčiražü is 'bringing along' (ab- 'take' plus a second verb; compare the published abčiraba and abčirarun), a converb. γatasun buγaγ̇u (Ming 板 枷) is 'board-cangue'; emüsgežü (Ming 帶着 'wearing') is a stem I do not know, with the converb -žü, 'putting on'. The name Qaldun-Burqan is printed with the two parts in reverse order; -(n)a is the dative-locative 'to'. žoriγ̇ulba is žori- 'point at' (Ming 指着行) with a causative -γ̇ul-: 'made go toward'.

sentences.t: Belgütei-jin eke tere ail-dur bijü keġen žaγ̇aγdažu Belgütei eke-jüġen abura odču
sentences.l: Belgütei's mother, that in-the-camp is, saying, being-told, Belgütei own-mother to-fetch, going,
sentences.i: Told that Belgütei's mother was in that camp, Belgütei went to fetch his own mother,
sentences.n: Belgütei-jin eke is 'Belgütei's mother', genitive -jin after a vowel. tere ail-dur bijü keġen is 'that, in the camp, there is, saying'. žaγ̇aγdažu is a passive converb (stem žaγ̇a- inferred from Ming 吿着 'telling'): 'being told', so someone told him, but no one is named. eke-jüġen is 'own mother' (Ming 母 自的行), with the front-vowel reflexive -jüġen. abura is ab- 'take' with a converb of purpose -ura, 'in order to take' (Ming 取), odču 'going'. The sentence runs on to the door.

sentences.t: "Köġüd min-u qād bolžuγ̇u keġegdemüi bi.
sentences.l: Sons my, sovereigns having-become, being-said, I.
sentences.i: "I am told my sons have become sovereigns.
sentences.n: köġüd is köġün 'son' with the plural -d. qād is the contracted plural of qaγan, 'sovereigns' (Ming 王子 'princes'). bolžuγ̇u is bol- 'become' in the past -žuγ̇u; keġegdemüi is keġe- 'say' with a passive -gde- and a present ending -müi (Ming 被說有), so 'am said (to be)'. The passive keeps the speakers unnamed: 'it is said of me'. This is the mother speaking.

sentences.t: Ende maγ̇ui küġün-dür tübežü edöġe köġüd(i)-jen niγ̇ur ker üžeküi bi"
sentences.l: Here bad man-to being-paired, now own-sons' face how to-see, I?"
sentences.i: Paired here with a bad man, how can I now look my sons in the face?"
sentences.n: tübežü (Ming 配着) is a stem I infer, 'being matched/paired', a converb. küġün-dür, 'to a man', is the dative-locative -dür after a front-vowel word, and maγ̇ui is 'bad'. köġüd(i)-jen niγ̇ur is 'own sons' face' (Ming 兒子每自的行 面); the (i) is Shiratori's. ker üžeküi bi: 'how to see, I?' (Ming 怎生 見), a rhetorical question: üžeküi is üže- with a participle -küi. The quotation closes on bi".

sentences.t: kēġed güjižü siγui-hoi-dur sirγužuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Having-said, running, in-the-dense-wood slipped-in.
sentences.i: With that she ran and slipped into the thick wood.
sentences.n: kēġed is keġe- 'say' with -ġed, written with a long ē (the two run together). güjižü is 'running'. siγui-hoi-dur is 'in the dense wood' (Ming 密林 裏); siγui-hoi is printed as one hyphenated word; the dative-locative -dur takes her in. sirγužuγ̇u is the printed spelling of širγu- 'squeeze, creep in' in the past -žuγ̇u.

sentences.t: Tedüi erižü ese oldalai.
sentences.l: Thus seeking, not found-was.
sentences.i: He searched for her but did not find her.
sentences.n: tedüi, 'thus, so, thereupon', and erižü 'seeking' (Ming 尋着). ese is the negative of a past action ('did not', against ülü for the present and future). oldalai (Ming 得有來) is ol- 'find' with a passive -da- and -lai; I read it as 'was not found', but the Ming 得 'got' gives the active, so 'he did not get her' is also possible.

not (negates a past action; ülü negates present or future) [不曾]

sentences.t: Belgütei nojan Merkidai ele jasutu küġün-(n)i eke-ji min-u abčira" keġežü γodolidqu büleġe.
sentences.l: Belgütei noyan, Merkidai, any bone-having man (acc.), mother (acc.) my "bring!" saying, to-be-shot-with-blunt-heads was.
sentences.i: Belgütei the noyan, calling "Bring my mother!", had every Merkid man "of bone" shot at with blunt-headed arrows.
sentences.n: The hardest unit of the part. Belgütei nojan (Ming 官人) is 'the noyan Belgütei'. Merkidai: Merkid with an ending -ai I cannot identify (Ming 種名). ele jasutu küġün-(n)i: jasu is 'bone' (Ming 骨頭的 'bone-having') and ele 'any, all' (Ming 但); 'bone' may mean lineage, so 'men of rank'. eke-ji min-u abčira is 'my mother, bring!', with abčira the bare stem as an imperative, and the closing quotation mark after it (the opening one is not printed). γodolidqu (Ming 敎𩪛頭射) is a stem I infer, 'shoot with blunt-headed arrows', with -d- 'cause' and a participle -qu, and büleġe 'used to be, was'. The sense is 'caused to be shot' but who shot whom is not clear to me.

sentences.t: Burqan-(n)i qučilduγsad γurban žaγ̇ud Merkid-i uruγ-un uruγ-a kürtele hünesü-ġer keistele ülidgebe.
sentences.l: Burqan (acc.) those-who-surrounded-together, three hundred Merkid (acc.), offspring's offspring-to until, ash-like scraping-as, destroyed.
sentences.i: They wiped out the three hundred Merkid who had ringed Burqan, down to their children's children, as one scrapes away ashes.
sentences.n: Burqan-(n)i is the mountain with the accusative; qučilduγsad is qučil- 'encircle' with -du- 'together' and the plural participle -γsad (Ming 相圍繞了的), 'those who surrounded together'; a plural participle standing before γurban žaγ̇ud Merkid-i names the group, 'the three hundred Merkid who had ringed Burqan' (the circling of unit 24 and of §§100–104), not a converb of the Mongols. Merkid-i is the accusative of the people, object of ülidgebe (Ming 殄絕了) 'made extinct', a stem I infer (compare ülüdgebe below). uruγ-un uruγ-a kürtele: 'to the offspring of the offspring' with kür- 'reach' and -tele 'until'. hünesü-ġer keistele is 'ash-like scraping': hünesü 'ash' with the instrumental -ġer, the same phrase as hünesü-ġer keisgen in the published §§87–92, 'as ash is scraped off' (Ming 灰行 刮般); the 'like' comes from the published use and the Ming 般 at keistele.

sentences.t: Hülegsed eme köġün an-u ebürikün metüs-i ebüridbe;
sentences.l: Remaining-ones, wife, son, their, to-be-embraced such (acc.) embraced;
sentences.i: Of the survivors, their wives and sons, such as were fit to be taken to the bosom, they took to the bosom;
sentences.n: Hülegsed is hüle- 'remain' with the plural participle -gsed (Ming 餘剩的), 'the ones left'; an-u is 'their', the back-vowel partner of in-ü, set after its noun. ebürikün (Ming 可懷抱的 'fit to be embraced') and ebüridbe (懷抱了) share the stem ebüri- from ebür 'bosom'; metüs-i is metü 'like, such' with the plural -s and accusative -i (Ming 般每 行), 'those of the sort'. The semicolon is Shiratori's.

sentences.i: and such as were fit to be brought in, they brought into their own households.

sentences.t: "Qān ečige min-u Žamuqa anda qojar-a nököčegdežü
sentences.l: "Qān, my father; Žamuqa anda: the two by being-accompanied,
sentences.i: "Having had the two as companions, Qan my father and Jamuqa my sworn brother,
sentences.n: Qān ečige min-u is 'Qan, my father'; Temüjin calls To'oril so. Žamuqa anda is 'Jamuqa the sworn brother'. qojar-a is the dative used for the doers after a passive, 'by the two'. nököčegdežü is nököče- 'be a companion' (from nökör) with the passive -gde- and the converb -žü (Ming 被做伴着 'being made companions'), so 'having been accompanied'. The speech runs through §113 as a single long sentence set out in short pieces: the converbs here lead to the verbs in the lines that follow.

sentences.t: teṅgiri γažar-a küčü nemegdežü
sentences.l: Heaven, to-earth, strength being-added,
sentences.i: with strength added by Heaven and Earth,
sentences.n: teṅgiri is 'Heaven' (Ming 天) with no ending, γažar-a is 'earth' with the dative-locative -a (Ming 地行), küčü is 'strength' (氣力). nemegdežü is neme- 'add' (stem inferred, Ming 被添着) with the passive -gde- and the converb -žü, 'being added'. The Mongol puts the case ending only on 'earth'; that the strength comes from both Heaven and Earth is my reading, and the English keeps it.

sentences.t: erketü teṅgiri-de nereidčü eke etügen-e kürgežü
sentences.l: Mighty, to-Heaven being-named, mother to-Etügen delivering,
sentences.i: invoked before mighty Heaven and brought to Mother Etügen,
sentences.n: erketü is erke 'power' with the possessive -tü (Ming 威勢有的 'with authority'), qualifying teṅgiri-de 'to Heaven'. nereidčü is nere- 'name' with something I cannot analyse (Ming 被題着 'being named / called on'); Etügen is the Earth (the Ming says 地 'ground') and eke etügen-e 'to Mother Etügen' is the dative. kürgežü is kürge- 'deliver', converb. Whether Temüjin is invoked, or his cause is, is not said; I use 'invoked' for the Ming's 'named'.

sentences.t: ere hačitu Merkid irgen-i ebür ba an-u hoγtorγou bolγaba.
sentences.l: Man, vengeance-having, Merkid people (acc.), bosom also their empty made.
sentences.i: As men with a vengeance to take, we have made the Merkid people's bosom empty,
sentences.n: ere hačitu (Ming 男子 讐報) is 'man, having a requital': hačitu is hači 'enmity' with the possessive -tu, so 'men of vengeance' or 'avengers'. The Merkid are named first with the accusative, and the nouns that follow are 'their' (an-u): the Merkid people, their bosom (ebür) 'also' (ba, Ming 也) emptied. bolγaba is bol- 'become' with the causative -γa- and the past -ba, 'made into'; hoγtorγou 'empty' is a variant spelling of hoγtorγu. The speaker turns the Merkid's own words in §105 back on them.

sentences.l: Kin's also men (acc.) made-to-cease, we;
sentences.i: we have ended their kin and their menfolk;
sentences.n: Uruγ-un küġün-(n)i is 'of the kin, the men (acc.)': uruγ 'offspring, descendants, kin' with the genitive -un and küġün 'man' with the accusative, so 'the men of their line'. ülüdgebe (Ming 敎廢了 'caused to abolish') is a stem I infer, ülüd- with something I cannot name, the verb of the line, and bida 'we'.

morph.gloss: genitive: of (back-vowel form, after a consonant)
accusative: marks the object (the (n) is Shiratori's)
to bring to an end, abolish (stem inferred; Ming 敎廢 'cause to be abolished') [敎廢了]
(uncertain; perhaps causative, as in the Ming 敎)

sentences.t: hülegsed-i ba anu arbilaba že bida.
sentences.l: The-remaining-ones (acc.) also their seized, indeed, we.
sentences.i: and the survivors, too, we have taken captive.
sentences.n: hülegsed-i is the plural participle of hüle- 'remain' (Ming 餘剩的) with the accusative, 'those left'. anu is the same an-u 'their', here printed without a hyphen. arbilaba (Ming 據要了) is a stem I infer, arbila- 'seize', in the past -ba. že (Ming 也者 'so be it') is a particle that ends the clause, and bida closes it. The full stop is Shiratori's.

morph.gloss: to remain, be left over (stem inferred; Ming 餘剩) [餘剩的(行)]
past participle with plural -d: those who ...-ed
their (back-vowel companion of in-ü, third-person genitive placed after its noun) [他的]
to seize, take captive (stem inferred; Ming 據要) [據要了]
particle, 'indeed, so' (Ming 也者 'so be it') [也者︀]

sentences.t: Merkid irgen-i tedüi busalγažu ičuja" keġeldübe.
sentences.l: Merkid people (acc.) that-much wrecking, let-us-withdraw" said-together.
sentences.i: We have broken the Merkid people thus far; let us withdraw," they said together.
sentences.n: Merkid irgen-i is the people with the accusative; tedüi, 'so much, thus far'. busalγažu is busal- 'ruin' (stem inferred; Ming 敎毀亂着) with a causative -γa- and the converb -žu. ičuja is a hortative in -ja (Ming 退咱 'let us withdraw'), the stem ič- being my reading. The quotation closes here; keġeldübe is keġe- 'say' with the reciprocal -ldü- and the past -be (共說了), 'said together', so the three agree. Whether Temüjin speaks the whole speech and the others agree, or all say it, is not clear.

morph.gloss: the Merkid, a people (people name) [種名]
people, the common folk of a camp or realm (noun) [百姓 行]
to be ruined, scattered (stem inferred; Ming 毀亂 'ruin and confuse') [敎毀亂着]
to withdraw, retreat (stem inferred; Ming 退) [退咱]

sentences.t: Uduid-Merkid dürberün
sentences.l: Uduid-Merkid hurrying-when,
sentences.i: When the Uduid Merkid fled in haste,
sentences.n: Uduid-Merkid is a clan name, the Uduid of the Merkid, with no case ending: the subject of the time clause. dürberün is dürbe- 'hurry' with the converb of time -rün (Ming 忙走時), 'when hurrying'. The clause continues into the child's description in the next unit.

morph.gloss: the Uduid Merkid, the Uduid clan of the Merkid (clan name) [姓(名)]
to hurry, flee in haste (stem inferred; Ming 忙走) [忙走時]

sentences.t: buluγan maqalaitu maral-un γodun γudusutu ičigin-žarγaγ usun-u buluγan žalγaγsan deġeltü
sentences.l: Sable cap-having, doe's hoof-skin boot-having, powder-skin water's sable spliced coat-having,
sentences.i: wearing a sable cap, boots of doe's hoof-skin, and a coat pieced together of water-sable and powder-skin,
sentences.n: A string of possessives, each one a thing the child is said to have: maqalaitu (maqalai 'cap' with -tu; Ming 帽兒有的), γudusutu (γudusu 'boot' with -tu; 靴子有的) and deġeltü (deġel 'coat' with the front-vowel -tü; 衣裳有的). maral-un is 'of the doe' (Ming 母鹿的), γodun is the hoof-skin (蹄皮). ičigin-žarγaγ (Ming 粉皮 'powder-skin') I cannot analyse. usun-u buluγan is 'sable of the water' (Ming 水的), which may be otter or beaver. žalγaγsan is žalγa- 'join' with the participle -γsan (Ming 接了的), 'pieced together'.

morph.gloss: cap, hat (noun; Ming 帽兒) [帽兒有的]
genitive: of (back-vowel form, after a consonant)
hoof-skin, hoof (noun; Ming 蹄皮) [蹄皮]
boot (noun; Ming 靴子) [靴子 有的]
'powder-skin', a fine dressed skin (Ming 粉皮; the compound is not analysed) [粉皮]
to join, splice (Ming 接) [接了的]

sentences.t: tabun nasutu Küčü neretü nidün-dür(i)-jen γaltu köġüken-i
sentences.l: Five aged, Küčü named, in-own-eyes fire-having child (acc.),
sentences.i: a child of five years, named Küchü, with fire in his eyes,
sentences.n: tabun nasutu is 'five aged' (nasu 'age' with -tu); Küčü neretü is 'named Küchü' (nere 'name' with -tü). nidün-dür(i)-jen γaltu is 'in his own eyes, fire-having' (Ming 眼 裏 自的行 (火)有的), the figure of a keen, bright-eyed boy; nidün-dür is the dative-locative and the reflexive-possessive -(i)jen follows. köġüken-i is köġü 'son, child' with the diminutive -ken and the accusative (Ming (小兒)行). The child is the object of the verbs that follow.

morph.gloss: age, years of life (noun) [歲 有的]
Küchü, a boy's name (personal name; Ming 人名) [人名]
possessive: having a name, named (front-vowel form)
reflexive-possessive: one's own (front-vowel form; the (i) is Shiratori's)

sentences.t: bidan-u čeriġüd nutuγ-tur qočoruγsan-i olžu abčiražü Höġelün eke-de soqa abču ögčü odba.
sentences.l: Our soldiers, in-the-camp abandoned-one (acc.) finding, bringing-along, to-Höġelün mother present taking, giving, went.
sentences.i: Our soldiers found him, left behind in the camp, brought him along, and went to give him to Mother Högelün as a present.
sentences.n: bidan-u čeriġüd is 'our soldiers' as before. nutuγ-tur qočoruγsan-i is 'the one abandoned in the camp' (Ming 營盤 裏 抛下的 行): nutuγ 'camping-ground' with the dative-locative -tur, qočor- 'fall behind' with the participle -γsan and the accusative. olžu, abčiražü are converbs, 'finding, bringing'. Höġelün eke-de has the dative -de, 'to Mother Högelün'. soqa (Ming 人事 'present') abču ögčü odba is 'taking a gift, giving, went'; I read it as presenting the child as a gift, but the order of the last three verbs is not certain. The part ends on this full stop.

morph.gloss: of us, our (bida 'we, inclusive', stem bidan-, + genitive -u) [咱的]
soldier, army (the vowel before the plural is Shiratori's linking -ü-) [軍每]
dative-locative: in (back-vowel form after a consonant)
to be left behind, abandoned (compare qočorba; Ming 抛下 'cast down') [抛下的 行]
to bring along (ab- 'take' plus a second verb; form uncertain) [將來着]
Högelün, a woman's name (personal name) [婦人名]
present, gift of courtesy (noun; Ming 人事) [人事]
